\section[il tirocinio]{il tirocinio — the internship, the traineeship}

\label{lesson:IT-C358-tirocinio}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for unemployed, then the Italian for the notice.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il tirocinio}
\textbf{il tirocinio} — \textquotedblleft{}the internship, the traineeship\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Faccio un tirocinio di tre mesi in uno studio di architetti.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I am doing a three-month internship in an architects' office.}
\end{quote}

Many people also say \emph{lo stage}, from French.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tirocinio} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{tīrōcinium} \textquotedblleft{}first military service, apprenticeship\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{tīrō} \textquotedblleft{}a young recruit\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il tirocinio}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il tirocinio}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{il tirocinio}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for unemployed, then the Italian for the notice, then say \emph{il tirocinio} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does il tirocinio mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The internship, the traineeship\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[il tirocinante]{il tirocinante — the intern, the trainee}

\label{lesson:IT-C358-tirocinante}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the notice, then the Italian for the internship.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il tirocinante}
\textbf{il tirocinante} — \textquotedblleft{}the intern, the trainee\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
I tirocinanti cominciano lunedì.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The interns start on Monday.}
\end{quote}

A woman is \emph{la tirocinante}; one form for both.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tirocinante} is built on \emph{tirocinio} \textquotedblleft{}internship\textquotedblright{}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{tīrōcinium} \textquotedblleft{}apprenticeship\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{tīrō} \textquotedblleft{}a recruit\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[l'apprendista]{l'apprendista — the apprentice}

\label{lesson:IT-C358-apprendista}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the internship, then the Italian for the intern.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'apprendista}
\textbf{l'apprendista} — \textquotedblleft{}the apprentice\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ho cominciato come apprendista in una panetteria.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I started as an apprentice in a bakery.}
\end{quote}

One form for a man or a woman: \emph{un apprendista, un'apprendista}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{apprendista} is built on \emph{apprendere} \textquotedblleft{}to learn\textquotedblright{}, which comes from Latin \emph{apprehendere} \textquotedblleft{}to seize, to grasp\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{prehendere} \textquotedblleft{}to take hold of\textquotedblright{}: learning is grasping.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{l'apprendista}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the internship, then the Italian for the intern, then say \emph{l'apprendista} again
\end{itemize}

\section[il datore di lavoro]{il datore di lavoro — the employer}

\label{lesson:IT-C358-datore-di-lavoro}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the intern, then the Italian for the apprentice.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il datore di lavoro}
\textbf{il datore di lavoro} — \textquotedblleft{}the employer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Il mio datore di lavoro mi paga il corso di inglese.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My employer pays for my English lessons.}
\end{quote}

Literally the giver of work. In speech people often say \emph{il capo} or \emph{l'azienda}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{datore} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{dator} \textquotedblleft{}a giver\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{dare} \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{}; \emph{lavoro} is built on \emph{lavorare}, inherited from Latin \emph{labōrāre} \textquotedblleft{}to toil\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il datore di lavoro}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il datore di lavoro}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{il datore di lavoro}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the intern, then the Italian for the apprentice, then say \emph{il datore di lavoro} again
\end{itemize}

\section[il dipendente]{il dipendente — the employee}

\label{lesson:IT-C358-dipendente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the apprentice, then the Italian for the employer.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il dipendente}
\textbf{il dipendente} — \textquotedblleft{}the employee\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
L'azienda ha cinquanta dipendenti.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The company has fifty employees.}
\end{quote}

As an adjective, \emph{lavoro dipendente} is salaried work. Built on \emph{dipendere}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dipendente} is the present participle of \emph{dipendere} \textquotedblleft{}to depend\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{dēpendēre} \textquotedblleft{}to hang from\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{pendēre} \textquotedblleft{}to hang\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il dipendente}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il dipendente}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{il dipendente}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the apprentice, then the Italian for the employer, then say \emph{il dipendente} again
\end{itemize}
